contract_plain_english: In the proof setting of independent, mean-zero, sub-exponential X_1,...,X_N, let S be their sum and let t ≥ 0. For every exponential-tilting parameter λ > 0, Markov's inequality followed by independence gives the one-sided bound P{S ≥ t} ≤ exp(-λt) product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i). This is exactly Equation (2.23) on PDF page 25/printed page 36; it is an intermediate upper-tail estimate and has neither an absolute value nor a prefactor 2.

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.8.1 proof paragraph immediately preceding Equation (2.23)
source_evidence.observation: The proof defines S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i and says to multiply S ≥ t by a parameter λ, exponentiate, and use Markov's inequality and independence, leading to the bound previously numbered (2.7).

The displayed equation is P{S ≥ t} ≤ e^{-λt} product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i). It is a one-sided upper-tail estimate, has no absolute value and no prefactor 2, and factors the MGF into one factor per summand.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.7) and the sentence following its subsequent substitution
source_evidence.observation: The earlier Chernoff argument gives the same Markov-and-independence product bound and explicitly states that it holds for any λ > 0. Equation (2.23) invokes this bound by number.
The inherited setting consists of independent, mean-zero, sub-exponential random variables X_1,...,X_N and a threshold t ≥ 0.

binders: N is the implicitly positive integer number of summands (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
X_1,...,X_N are real random variables on a common implicit probability space (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement and proof).
S abbreviates sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, opening proof sentence).
t is the nonnegative real threshold inherited from Theorem 2.8.1 (PDF page 25/printed page 36, theorem statement).
λ is a positive real exponential-tilting parameter; positivity is inherited from the referenced Equation (2.7) argument (PDF page 8/printed page 19, sentence stating the bound holds for any λ > 0).
conclusions: P{S ≥ t} ≤ exp(-λt) product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
definitions_and_conventions: S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, opening proof sentence).
E exp(λX_i) is the moment generating function of X_i at λ (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) and the following paragraph).
The product ranges over every index i = 1,...,N and arises from independence (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) and its introducing sentence).
The left event is the one-sided event S ≥ t, not the two-sided event |S| ≥ t (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
hypotheses: X_1,...,X_N are jointly independent (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement and the proof's explicit use of independence).

The enclosing theorem also assumes every X_i is mean zero and sub-exponential, although those properties are not used in the Markov-and-factorization step itself (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
λ > 0 (PDF page 8/printed page 19, the Equation (2.7) argument expressly stating its range).
implicit_context: The inequality is the exponential Markov bound after multiplying S ≥ t by λ > 0 and exponentiating (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph before Equation (2.23); PDF page 8/printed page 19, Equation (2.7) derivation).
Joint independence is used to replace E exp(λ sum_i X_i) by product_i E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph before Equation (2.23)).
The mean-zero and sub-exponential assumptions become relevant only in the next step, where each individual MGF is bounded (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph following Equation (2.23)).

details: Equation (2.23) bounds only P{S ≥ t}; it contains no absolute value and no lower-tail event (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The factor 2 appearing in the final theorem is absent from this intermediate upper-tail estimate (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23) versus Theorem 2.8.1 statement).
The estimate is valid for each λ > 0, with t ≥ 0 inherited from the theorem (PDF page 8/printed page 19, Equation (2.7) discussion; PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
No optimization or small-λ restriction has yet been imposed at Equation (2.23); the small-λ constraint appears next as Equation (2.24) (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The right side is exactly exp(-λt) times a product of N individual MGFs (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
Independence, rather than identical distribution, supplies the product; the X_i may have different laws (PDF page 25/printed page 36, theorem statement and proof).

undebatable_constraints: The left side is P{S ≥ t}, a one-sided non-strict upper-tail event, with S = sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The exponential prefactor is exactly exp(-λt) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The remaining right-hand factor is exactly product_{i=1}^N E exp(λX_i) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.23)).
The parameter λ is positive, as inherited from the explicitly referenced Equation (2.7) argument (PDF page 8/printed page 19).
Independence is essential to the product factorization (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph introducing Equation (2.23)).
There is no absolute value around S and no numeric prefactor 2 in Equation (2.23) (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
